impl.residual_risk: Every change is in rendering, text cleaning or caveat emission; no ranking, ordering, comparator key, relevance score, selection path or retrieval RPC was touched, and no src/lib/rag/** source file was edited (the one new file there is a test). Proof run locally and offline: the full unit suite, 954 files / 12348 tests, all green, plus eslint and tsc -p tsconfig.typecheck.json clean. Three residual risks worth naming. (1) M8 widens the "not locally validated" caveat from the literal status "unverified" to anything that is not locally_reviewed or approved, so more answers will now carry that warning badge and more sources will show it — severity stays "warning", so no answer that previously succeeded is now refused, but the visible caveat rate on partially-enriched documents will rise; that is the conservative direction the governance doc asks for, and it is deliberately not fed back into retrieval (Refutation 3). The matching asymmetry in src/lib/clinical-review-queue.ts:87 is unfixed because that file is outside this package. (2) H3 now drops a whole column when its header cleans to empty; the normalizer never emits an empty header (it synthesizes "Details N"/"Column N"), so only a header that was pure provenance can trigger it, but a table whose header was genuinely only a page or file reference over clinical values would lose that column rather than misalign it — misalignment was the graver hazard. (3) L111 cuts at a word boundary, and because the trailing "..." is normalised away downstream, a truncated Safety chip can now end at a sentence boundary with no visible truncation marker; that was already true before this change (the marker was collapsed to a full stop), and the chip still carries its citation link. Not run, by the package's own rules: npm run verify:pr-local and the offline RAG eval steps its classifier would add (eval:rag:offline, eval:rag:adversarial:offline) because source-governance.ts sets rag_eval_changed; CI must run them. No provider-backed command was executed.

M8 widening is exactly the finding's scope, not wider: `normalizeSourceMetadata` (src/lib/source-metadata.ts:68-73) already defaults a null/absent status to "unverified", so sources with no metadata got the caveat before and after (probe: null => [unverified_source], {} => [unverified_source]); only the literal "unknown" changes. Registry rows cannot carry "unknown" (migrations pin `validation_status in ('unverified','locally_reviewed','approved')`), so registry-backed answers are unaffected in live data. Minor wording inconsistency worth a follow-up: the per-source badge label (`validationStatusLabel`, source-metadata.ts:141) still says "Validation unknown" while the answer-level warning now says "have not been locally validated"; and evidence-panels.tsx:1043 / clinical-review-queue.ts:87 still compare `=== "unverified"` only (outside this package, already flagged by the implementer).

M9 note (non-blocking): the new regex `\b(?:[Pp]rocedure|[Pp]olicy|[Pp]rotocol)\s+(?=[A-Z0-9/-]*\d)[A-Z]{2,}(?:-[A-Z0-9]+)+...` with only the `g` flag no longer scrubs an all-caps keyword ("PROCEDURE PAE-PRO-0338/16", "POLICY MH-POL-0012"), so the code comment at src/lib/clinical-safety.ts:82-83 ("The keyword stays case-insensitive by spelling") is inaccurate. In a probe through extractSafetyFindings the upstream sanitizer already removed both all-caps examples, so the practical effect is small and the audit's own fix sketch sanctioned dropping `i`; if desired, add `PROCEDURE|POLICY|PROTOCOL` to the alternation. Pre-existing and unchanged: a genuine token like "protocol ANC-1500" is still scrubbed because it is upper-case with a digit.

L111 note (non-blocking, pre-existing): `truncateAtSafeBoundary` never splits a token, but the appended "..." is normalised by `sanitizeAnswerText` — probe: "Target serum lithium level 0.6..." => "Target serum lithium level 0.6." and a trailing orphan fragment ("and ANC...") is dropped entirely. So a truncated Safety chip still reads as a complete sentence, and a value can be cut from its unit at the word boundary. This was already true before the change (implementer's residual risk 3); a follow-up could prefer the last sentence terminator inside the window when one exists.

L19 note: the fix follows the package note (strip pointer with its brackets) rather than the finding's alternative (keep the pointer for verification). `emptyBracketPattern` sweeps any empty `()`/`[]` pair in every clinicalOnly cell, including pairs not produced by the scrub — acceptable for clinical tables. The bracketed pattern also absorbs an optional leading "see" ("(see page 3)").

H3 note: the chosen remedy drops the blanked column entirely (permitted by the package note; body values under it are removed rather than shifted).
